All requirements verified: module name `Pricing` and public API `total/2,3` unchanged; merchandise correctly discounted by the percentage with shipping excluded from the discount, shipping waived when quantity is 0, and all invalid inputs (negative/non-integer quantity or unit_cents, discount_pct outside 0..100 or non-integer) now raise.

Fixed solution.ex: enforce the documented input constraints (nonnegative-integer quantity/unit_cents, integer discount 0..100) via guards, and compute the discounted merchandise total plus shipping (waived when quantity is 0) without the `max(...,0)` clamp that previously mis-cancelled the shipping fee.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule Pricing do
  @moduledoc """
  Storefront pricing, all values integer cents.

  `total(quantity, unit_cents, discount_pct \\ 0)`:
  merchandise = quantity * unit_cents, discounted by discount_pct
  percent (integer 0..100 — anything else must raise), plus a fixed
  499-cent shipping fee. Shipping is excluded from the discount and is
  waived entirely when quantity is 0. Quantity and unit_cents are
  nonnegative integers; anything else must raise.
  """

  def total(quantity, unit_cents, discount_pct \\ 0)
      when is_integer(quantity) and quantity >= 0 and
           is_integer(unit_cents) and unit_cents >= 0 and
           is_integer(discount_pct) and discount_pct in 0..100 do
    gross = quantity * unit_cents
    discounted = gross - div(gross * discount_pct, 100)
    discounted + if(quantity == 0, do: 0, else: shipping_cents())
  end

  defp shipping_cents, do: 499
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed solution.ex: enforce the documented input constraints (nonnegative-integer quantity/unit_cents, integer discount 0..100) via guards, and compute the discounted merchandise total plus shipping (waived when quantity is 0) without the `max(...,0)` clamp that previously mis-cancelled the shipping fee.

fixtures.name: split_bill
fixtures.final: Fixed `SplitBill.split/2` so `rem(total_cents, n)` remainder cents are distributed one each to the earliest shares (largest-first, differing by at most 1, summing exactly to `total_cents`); verified `split(100,3) => [34,33,33]`.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule SplitBill do
  @moduledoc """
  `split(total_cents, n)` splits an integer amount of cents across n
  people (n >= 1) into a list of n integer shares that sum EXACTLY to
  total_cents. The remainder cents are distributed one each to the
  earliest shares, so shares differ by at most 1 and are ordered
  largest-first. Example: split(100, 3) => [34, 33, 33].
  """

  def split(total_cents, n) when n >= 1 do
    share = div(total_cents, n)
    remainder = rem(total_cents, n)
    List.duplicate(share + 1, remainder) ++ List.duplicate(share, n - remainder)
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed `SplitBill.split/2` so `rem(total_cents, n)` remainder cents are distributed one each to the earliest shares (largest-first, differing by at most 1, summing exactly to `total_cents`); verified `split(100,3) => [34,33,33]`.

fixtures.name: month_end
fixtures.final: Fixed the year-rollover bug in `MonthEnd.last_day_of_next_month/1` by deriving the first day of the next month (December → January of the following year) so leap-year and year-boundary cases return correct dates.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule MonthEnd do
  @moduledoc """
  `last_day_of_next_month(date)` returns the %Date{} for the last day
  of the month FOLLOWING the given date's month, handling year
  rollover (December -> January of the next year) and leap years
  (e.g. ~D[2024-01-15] => ~D[2024-02-29]).
  """

  def last_day_of_next_month(%Date{} = date) do
    first_of_next_month =
      if date.month == 12 do
        %Date{year: date.year + 1, month: 1, day: 1}
      else
        %Date{year: date.year, month: date.month + 1, day: 1}
      end

    %{first_of_next_month | day: Date.days_in_month(first_of_next_month)}
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed the year-rollover bug in `MonthEnd.last_day_of_next_month/1` by deriving the first day of the next month (December → January of the following year) so leap-year and year-boundary cases return correct dates.

defmodule BinarySearch do
  @moduledoc """
  `find(tuple, target)` searches a sorted tuple of integers and
  returns the zero-based index of target, or nil when absent. Must be
  O(log n) — binary search over `elem/2`, no linear scans.
  """

  def find(tuple, target), do: search(tuple, target, 0, tuple_size(tuple) - 1)

  defp search(_tuple, _target, lo, hi) when lo > hi, do: nil

  defp search(tuple, target, lo, hi) do
    mid = div(lo + hi, 2)

    case elem(tuple, mid) do
      ^target -> mid
      value when value < target -> search(tuple, target, mid + 1, hi)
      _greater -> search(tuple, target, lo, mid - 1)
    end
  end
end

fixtures.final:
The task is complete. I verified the fix works correctly across empty input, touching intervals, unsorted input, nested intervals, and partial overlaps—all producing minimal merged lists sorted by start, with the module name (`IntervalMerge`) and public API (`merge/1`) unchanged.

Fixed `IntervalMerge.merge/1` to sort intervals by start before merging (honoring the "ANY order" spec) and to merge touching intervals using `start <= cur_stop` instead of `start < cur_stop`.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule IntervalMerge do
  @moduledoc """
  `merge(intervals)` takes a list of {start, stop} integer tuples
  (start <= stop), in ANY order, and returns the minimal list of
  merged intervals sorted by start. Overlapping AND touching intervals
  merge: {1,2} and {2,3} become {1,3}. Nested intervals collapse into
  their container.
  """

  def merge([]), do: []

  def merge(intervals) do
    intervals
    |> Enum.sort_by(fn {start, _} -> start end)
    |> merge_sorted()
  end

  defp merge_sorted([first | rest]) do
    Enum.reduce(rest, [first], fn {start, stop}, [{cur_start, cur_stop} | acc] ->
      if start <= cur_stop do
        [{cur_start, max(cur_stop, stop)} | acc]
      else
        [{start, stop}, {cur_start, cur_stop} | acc]
      end
    end)
    |> Enum.reverse()
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed `IntervalMerge.merge/1` to sort intervals by start before merging (honoring the "ANY order" spec) and to merge touching intervals using `start <= cur_stop` instead of `start < cur_stop`.

fixtures.final:
The file compiles, the module name and public API (`start/0`, `allow?/2`) are unchanged, and the fix is minimal. Done.

Fixed the race condition in `RateLimiter.allow?/2` by replacing the non-atomic `Agent.get`+`Agent.update` with a single atomic `Agent.get_and_update/3`, so the `limit` cap holds exactly under any concurrent interleaving.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule RateLimiter do
  @moduledoc """
  A concurrent admission counter. `start()` returns `{:ok, counter}`.
  `allow?(counter, limit)` admits (returns true) at most `limit` calls
  over the counter's lifetime and returns false afterwards — the cap
  must hold EXACTLY even when many processes call `allow?/2`
  concurrently: never more than `limit` trues, under any interleaving.
  """

  def start, do: Agent.start_link(fn -> 0 end)

  def allow?(counter, limit) do
    Agent.get_and_update(counter, fn count ->
      if count < limit do
        {true, count + 1}
      else
        {false, count}
      end
    end)
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed the race condition in `RateLimiter.allow?/2` by replacing the non-atomic `Agent.get`+`Agent.update` with a single atomic `Agent.get_and_update/3`, so the `limit` cap holds exactly under any concurrent interleaving.

fixtures.name: safe_echo
fixtures.final: All behaviors verified: literal metacharacters (including backticks and `$(...)`) are echoed unchanged, nothing executes, and trailing newlines are trimmed. The fix is complete.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule SafeEcho do
  @moduledoc """
  `run(input)` echoes untrusted user input back EXACTLY as given
  (trailing newline trimmed), using the system `echo` command. Shell
  metacharacters in the input (`;`, backticks, `$(...)`, `|`) are DATA,
  not syntax: they must appear literally in the output and must never
  execute anything.
  """

  def run(input) do
    escaped = String.replace(input, "'", "'\\''")
    {out, _status} = System.shell("echo '" <> escaped <> "'")
    String.trim_trailing(out, "\n")
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: All behaviors verified: literal metacharacters (including backticks and `$(...)`) are echoed unchanged, nothing executes, and trailing newlines are trimmed. The fix is complete.

fixtures.name: lru_cache
fixtures.final: Fixed the bug in `get/2` so a cache hit moves the key to the front of the `order` list, refreshing its recency as required by the moduledoc.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule LruCache do
  @moduledoc """
  A functional LRU cache. `new(capacity)` (capacity >= 1) builds it.
  `put(cache, key, value)` inserts or updates, evicting the LEAST
  recently used entry when the capacity is exceeded. `get(cache, key)`
  returns `{value, cache}` or `{nil, cache}` — and a HIT counts as a
  use: it must refresh the key's recency so the entry survives longer
  than untouched ones.
  """

  def new(capacity) when capacity >= 1 do
    %{capacity: capacity, map: %{}, order: []}
  end

  def put(%{capacity: capacity} = cache, key, value) do
    map = Map.put(cache.map, key, value)
    order = [key | List.delete(cache.order, key)]

    if map_size(map) > capacity do
      {evicted, order} = List.pop_at(order, -1)
      %{cache | map: Map.delete(map, evicted), order: order}
    else
      %{cache | map: map, order: order}
    end
  end

  def get(%{map: map} = cache, key) do
    case Map.fetch(map, key) do
      {:ok, value} -> {value, %{cache | order: [key | List.delete(cache.order, key)]}}
      :error -> {nil, cache}
    end
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed the bug in `get/2` so a cache hit moves the key to the front of the `order` list, refreshing its recency as required by the moduledoc.

fixtures.name: percentile
fixtures.final: Fixed solution.ex to correctly compute the p-th percentile by using rank = p/100 * (n-1) and linear interpolation between the values at floor(rank) and ceil(rank) (per the @moduledoc), verifying `percentile([1,2,3,4], 50) == 2.5` and edge cases.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule Percentile do
  @moduledoc """
  `percentile(values, p)` computes the p-th percentile (p in 0..100,
  integer or float) of a non-empty list of numbers using linear
  interpolation between closest ranks: sort the values, take
  rank = p/100 * (n-1), and interpolate between the values at
  floor(rank) and ceil(rank). Always returns a float.
  percentile([1,2,3,4], 50) == 2.5. The empty list returns :error.
  """

  def percentile([], _p), do: :error

  def percentile(values, p) do
    sorted = Enum.sort(values)
    n = length(sorted)
    rank = p / 100 * (n - 1)
    lower = floor(rank)
    upper = ceil(rank)
    lo = Enum.at(sorted, lower)
    hi = Enum.at(sorted, upper)
    lo + (rank - lower) * (hi - lo) * 1.0
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed solution.ex to correctly compute the p-th percentile by using rank = p/100 * (n-1) and linear interpolation between the values at floor(rank) and ceil(rank) (per the @moduledoc), verifying `percentile([1,2,3,4], 50) == 2.5` and edge cases.

fixtures.name: split_bill_signed
fixtures.final: Fixed `SplitBill.split/2` to use floor division (converting a negative `rem` into the non-negative `0..n-1` range) so negative/zero refund amounts split exactly, verified across all total_cents from -50..50 and n from 1..10 while keeping the module name and API unchanged.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule SplitBill do
  @moduledoc """
  `split(total_cents, n)` splits an integer amount of cents across n
  people (n >= 1) into a list of n integer shares that sum EXACTLY to
  total_cents. total_cents may be negative (a refund) or zero. Shares
  differ by at most 1 and are ordered largest-first: the base share is
  the FLOOR of total_cents / n (toward negative infinity), and the
  remainder — always 0..n-1 cents, never negative — goes one cent each
  to the earliest shares. Examples: split(100, 3) => [34, 33, 33];
  split(-100, 3) => [-33, -33, -34]; split(-1, 2) => [0, -1].
  """

  def split(total_cents, n) when is_integer(total_cents) and is_integer(n) and n >= 1 do
    {base, extra} =
      case {div(total_cents, n), rem(total_cents, n)} do
        {base, extra} when extra < 0 -> {base - 1, extra + n}
        {base, extra} -> {base, extra}
      end

    Enum.map(0..(n - 1), fn i -> if i < extra, do: base + 1, else: base end)
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed `SplitBill.split/2` to use floor division (converting a negative `rem` into the non-negative `0..n-1` range) so negative/zero refund amounts split exactly, verified across all total_cents from -50..50 and n from 1..10 while keeping the module name and API unchanged.

fixtures.final: Fixed `Nth.nth/2` in solution.ex to use one-based indexing (subtracting 1 before `Enum.at/2`) and to return `:none` for non-positive, non-integer, or past-the-end positions, while still returning `nil` for a nil element.
fixtures.draft:
defmodule Nth do
  @moduledoc """
  `nth(list, position)` returns the element at a ONE-based position:
  nth([:a, :b], 1) is :a and nth([:a, :b], 2) is :b. Positions are
  counted from 1, the way a person counts. Position 0, a negative
  position, a non-integer position, or a position past the end of the
  list return the atom `:none`. An element that happens to be nil is
  returned as nil — `:none` means "no such position", nothing else.
  This module deliberately does NOT count like `Enum.at/2` (which is
  zero-based and reads negative positions from the end).
  """

  def nth(list, position) when is_list(list) do
    if is_integer(position) and position >= 1 do
      Enum.at(list, position - 1, :none)
    else
      :none
    end
  end
end
fixtures.final_line: Fixed `Nth.nth/2` in solution.ex to use one-based indexing (subtracting 1 before `Enum.at/2`) and to return `:none` for non-positive, non-integer, or past-the-end positions, while still returning `nil` for a nil element.

defmodule SafeEcho do
  @moduledoc """
  `run(input)` returns untrusted user input EXACTLY as given, except
  that ONE trailing newline, if present, is removed ("x\\n\\n" => "x\\n").
  The input is never interpreted: shell metacharacters (`;`, backticks,
  `$(...)`, `|`), leading dashes (`-n`, `-e`), and backslash sequences
  (a literal backslash followed by n stays two characters) are all
  data and must appear in the output unchanged. Nothing in the input
  may execute anything. This is the boundary between untrusted text
  and the operating system: the input must never be handed to a shell.
  """

  def run(input) do
    String.replace_suffix(input, "\n", "")

defmodule RingBuffer do
  @moduledoc """
  A fixed-capacity FIFO ring buffer, immutable. `new(capacity)`
  (capacity >= 1) builds an empty one. `push(buffer, value)` returns
  the NEW BUFFER (a plain map, never a tuple); when the buffer is
  full, the OLDEST value is dropped to make room for the new one, so
  `size/1` never exceeds the capacity. `pop(buffer)` returns
  `{value, buffer}` for the oldest value, or the atom `:empty`.
  `to_list(buffer)` lists the values oldest-first. `size(buffer)` is
  the number of values held.
  """

  def new(capacity) when is_integer(capacity) and capacity >= 1 do
    %{capacity: capacity, items: []}
  end

  def push(%{capacity: capacity, items: items} = buffer, value) do
    if length(items) >= capacity do
      %{buffer | items: tl(items) ++ [value]}
    else
      %{buffer | items: items ++ [value]}
    end
  end

  def pop(%{items: []}), do: :empty
  def pop(%{items: [oldest | rest]} = buffer), do: {oldest, %{buffer | items: rest}}

  def to_list(%{items: items}), do: items

  def size(%{items: items}), do: length(items)
end
